# CLI reference

<!-- Generated by `make cli-docs` from cmd/twd's commands table and flag sets. Do not edit. -->

Every `twd` command and subcommand with its `--help` output: the usage line
and each flag with its default. `twd help` lists the commands by group;
`twd <command> --help` prints one of these sections. Every command also
takes `--state-dir` (default `$TWD_STATE_DIR` or `~/.twd`) and `--json`
([cli-json.md](cli-json.md)).

## Set up

### twd up

start twd on this machine

```text
twd up: start twd on this machine (one process: mgmt + embedded host; --separate-host for the two-node layout); an OAuth client of your tailnet mints every node key (Headscale: its API key)

usage: twd up --oauth-client-file <file> [--service] [--yes]  |  up --control=headscale --control-url <url> --tailnet <base_domain> --api-key-file <file> [--policy-apply]

flags:
  -allow-sibling-egress
    	let objects reach other objects on this host over the tailnet (hairpin; single-host tests and demos)
  -api-key-file string
    	--control=headscale only: 0600 file with HEADSCALE_API_KEY=… (read at use, never copied). Tailscale API keys are not a mint mode: use --oauth-client-file
  -control string
    	control-plane profile: tailscale, or headscale (ADR-015: a Headscale server at --control-url; --api-key-file holds HEADSCALE_API_KEY=…, --tailnet is its dns.base_domain) (default "tailscale")
  -control-url string
    	coordination server for the tailnet's nodes (default "https://controlplane.tailscale.com")
  -device-delete-delay duration
    	delete a killed object's device this long after the kill (< --kill-tombstone) (default 8s)
  -ephemeral
    	join object nodes as ephemeral; 'twd down' then deletes every device (tests, demos)
  -heartbeat duration
    	host heartbeat period (default 1s)
  -host-id string
    	this host's ID (default "h-<hostname>")
  -hostname-prefix string
    	prefix for every object node hostname (default "twd-")
  -insecure-shared-host
    	on a host without a process sandbox (Linux without Landlock), still serve process-tier workloads of more than one tenant; tenants are then NOT isolated from each other
  -json
    	machine-readable output
  -kill-tombstone duration
    	keep a killed node answering object_killed this long (default 12s)
  -local-dev
    	DEVELOPMENT ONLY: hostd and the CLI use mgmt's unix socket with the per-host token instead of the tailnet (hermetic tests). Normal operation is tsnet only
  -mgmt-authkey-file string
    	TS_AUTHKEY=… file for mgmt's node (unattended join: tests, automation); default: the tenant's credential mints it
  -mgmt-hostname string
    	mgmt's own tailnet node name (default twd-mgmt)
  -oauth-client-file string
    	mint mode "oauth" (Tailscale): 0600 file with TS_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID=… and TS_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET=tskey-client-… (an OAuth client with Auth Keys write, tag tag:twd). No browser, no Funnel
  -policy-apply
    	headscale: apply the policy snippet (validated first, written with If-Match); default: print it
  -pool-nodes int
    	pre-joined nodes kept per hot class (a create here in the last hour), so a new object is renamed onto one (~0.2 s) instead of joining a new node; each is a device (0 = off) (default 1)
  -port-mapping
    	use UPnP/NAT-PMP/PCP for this host's nodes (off by default: it adds ~250 ms to every new node's join and has every node ask the router for a mapping; turn on behind hard NATs that need router-assisted direct paths)
  -push-port int
    	port on this host's own tailnet node where mgmt pushes kills (--separate-host) (default 7474)
  -separate-host
    	run twd-hostd as its own process on its own tag:twd-host tailnet node (the scale-out layout; default: ONE process, the host agent embedded in twd-mgmt, mgmt's node the only infrastructure device). --local-dev implies it
  -service
    	run the supervisor as a service that starts at login: Linux systemd user unit (~/.config/systemd/user/twd.service), macOS LaunchAgent (~/Library/LaunchAgents/dev.twd.up.plist)
  -state-dir string
    	state directory (default $TWD_STATE_DIR or ~/.twd)
  -tailnet string
    	the tailnet to serve (oauth: read from the client's devices or mgmt's node; headscale: required, the dns.base_domain). Overrides discovery
  -tsapi-url string
    	Tailscale API base URL (testing)
  -warm-keys int
    	pre-minted single-use keys kept per (tenant, tag set), so a new object skips the key-API call; sized from the recent create rate, capped here (0 = off) (default 5)
  -workerd string
    	workerd binary
  -yes
    	non-interactive: don't ask for confirmation
```

### twd down

stop everything twd up started

```text
twd down: stop everything twd up started (--purge: kill every object and delete its device first)

usage: twd down [--purge] [--service]

flags:
  -json
    	machine-readable output
  -purge
    	kill every live object (audit: "twd down --purge") and delete its device before stopping (default with --ephemeral)
  -service
    	also disable and remove the service installed by twd up --service (systemd user unit / macOS LaunchAgent)
  -state-dir string
    	state directory (default $TWD_STATE_DIR or ~/.twd)
```

### twd link

use a remote twd-mgmt from this machine

```text
twd link: developer machine: use a remote twd-mgmt over your own Tailscale connection (WhoIs identity; no key or token)

usage: twd link [twd-mgmt.<tailnet>.ts.net] [--unlink]

flags:
  -control-url string
    	--tsnet: control URL for the CLI node (default "https://controlplane.tailscale.com")
  -json
    	machine-readable output
  -login-timeout duration
    	--tsnet: how long to wait for the browser login (default 5m0s)
  -state-dir string
    	state directory (default $TWD_STATE_DIR or ~/.twd)
  -tsnet
    	this machine has no Tailscale: the CLI runs its own ephemeral tsnet node (state under <state>/cli, interactive login the first time; your login is the identity mgmt sees)
  -tsnet-authkey-file string
    	--tsnet: TS_AUTHKEY=… file for an unattended first join (tests); default: interactive login
  -tsnet-dir string
    	--tsnet: node state dir (default <state>/cli); tests pass one explicitly
  -tsnet-hostname string
    	--tsnet: the CLI node's hostname (default twd-cli-<user>)
  -tsnet-tags string
    	--tsnet: comma-separated tags the CLI node advertises (tests)
  -unlink
    	forget the linked mgmt
```

### twd tenant

serve, list, update or remove tenants

```text
twd tenant: serve another tenant (its own tailnet) from this host; list, update (PATCH) or remove tenants

usage: twd tenant add <tailnet> --oauth-client-file <file> [--policy-apply] | tenant ls | tenant set <tenant> [--max-objects N] [--registrations-per-minute N] [--pool P] [--tier T] [--oauth-client-file FILE] [--max-containers N] [--max-container-mem-mib N] [--max-container-vcpu F] [--public-ingress allow|deny] | tenant rm <tenant> [--force]
  (every command takes --state-dir, default ~/.twd, and --json)
```

#### twd tenant add

```text
flags:
  -api-key-file string
    	--control=headscale only: 0600 file with HEADSCALE_API_KEY=…; read at use, never copied
  -control string
    	control-plane profile: tailscale, or headscale (ADR-015: a Headscale server at --control-url; the tailnet argument is its dns.base_domain) (default "tailscale")
  -control-url string
    	coordination server for this tailnet's nodes (default "https://controlplane.tailscale.com")
  -json
    	machine-readable output
  -oauth-client-file string
    	this tailnet's OAuth client (mint mode "oauth"): 0600 file with TS_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID=… and TS_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET=tskey-client-… (Auth Keys write, tag tag:twd); read at use, never copied
  -policy-apply
    	apply the base policy snippet (validated first, written with If-Match); default: print it
  -registrations-per-minute int
    	this tenant's node registration throttle (default 200/min)
  -state-dir string
    	state directory (default $TWD_STATE_DIR or ~/.twd)
```

#### twd tenant ls

```text
flags:
  -json
    	machine-readable output
  -state-dir string
    	state directory (default $TWD_STATE_DIR or ~/.twd)
```

#### twd tenant rm

```text
flags:
  -force
    	kill every live object (cascade) and purge before deleting
  -json
    	machine-readable output
  -state-dir string
    	state directory (default $TWD_STATE_DIR or ~/.twd)
```

#### twd tenant set

```text
flags:
  -json
    	machine-readable output
  -max-container-mem-mib int
    	containers: total guest memory quota (MiB)
  -max-container-vcpu float
    	containers: total vCPU quota (fractional, e.g. 2.5)
  -max-containers int
    	containers (ADR-032): running containers quota
  -max-objects int
    	object quota
  -oauth-client-file string
    	switch the tenant to mint mode oauth with this 0600 OAuth client file (on this host; read at use, never copied)
  -pool string
    	host pool the tenant's deployments are placed on ("-" = any host)
  -public-ingress string
    	public (Funnel) ingress gate for twd.jsonc "public" routes: allow | deny (ADR-029)
  -registrations-per-minute int
    	node registration throttle
  -state-dir string
    	state directory (default $TWD_STATE_DIR or ~/.twd)
  -tier string
    	default isolation tier: process | microvm ("-" = unset)
```

### twd doctor

check this machine can run twd

```text
twd doctor: check this machine: workerd runs, bundler offline, ~/.twd writable, the mint credential works, process sandbox active, system tailscaled not used; on Linux also glibc, kernel/Landlock ABI, KVM, firecracker, cgroups v2, systemd and the microVM tier

usage: twd doctor

flags:
  -json
    	machine-readable output
  -state-dir string
    	state directory (default $TWD_STATE_DIR or ~/.twd)
```

### twd host

add, list, remove or set up hosts

```text
twd host: add a remote host (mgmt mints its single-use tag:twd-host join key), list or remove hosts; cordon (no new placements), uncordon, or drain one (move its workloads elsewhere); install the microVM tier's helper; check a microVM

usage: twd host add <host-id> [--tenant <tailnet>] [--out <file>] | host ls | host rm <host-id> [--drain] | host cordon <host-id> | host uncordon <host-id> | host drain <host-id> [--allow-local-state-loss] [--dry-run] | host setup --microvm [--user <name>] [--hugepages N] | host setup --undo   (Linux, with sudo, once) | host vmcheck <workload> [--keyscan] [--container <Class>/<name>]
  (every command takes --state-dir, default ~/.twd, and --json)
```

```text
flags:
  -json

  -out string

  -state-dir string
    	state directory (default $TWD_STATE_DIR or ~/.twd)
  -tenant string
    	tenant: its tailnet, tenant ID or tailnet label (default: the 'twd up' tenant)
```

```text
flags:
```

## Develop

### twd init

create an app from a template

```text
twd init: create an app from a template (node-workflow needs Node.js on the deploying machine)

usage: twd init <dir> [--template hello|agent|mcp|ai-agent|lock|refund-approval|node-workflow] [--name <workload>]

flags:
  -json
    	machine-readable output
  -keep-tags
    	keep the template's tags instead of naming them after the app (tag:twd-wl-<workload>, tag:twd-<workload>-<class>)
  -name string
    	workload name (default: the directory name)
  -state-dir string
    	state directory (default $TWD_STATE_DIR or ~/.twd)
  -template string
    	hello | agent | mcp | ai-agent | lock | refund-approval | node-workflow (default "hello")
```

### twd dev

run an app locally, no tailnet

```text
twd dev: run an app locally: process tier + embedded control plane (no tailnet)

usage: twd dev [dir] [--port 8787] [--caller <name>[=<tag>,…]]… [--env <name>] [--wrangler | --from-wrangler-out <dir>]

flags:
  -caller value
    	an extra identity: its own dev node (tagged with =tag:a,tag:b) and local URL, listed in the result (repeatable)
  -console-port int
    	serve the read-only data console (KV keys, D1 rows) on 127.0.0.1:<port>; 0 picks a free port, -1 turns it off (devconsole.go)
  -env string
    	wrangler environment: use env.<name> from the wrangler config, as 'wrangler --env' does (the workload is named <name>-<env> unless the env sets a name)
  -from-wrangler-out string
    	deploy a bundle wrangler already built (the --outdir of 'wrangler deploy --dry-run')
  -inspector-port int
    	serve workerd's V8 inspector on 127.0.0.1:<port> for Chrome DevTools or VS Code (devinspector.go)
  -json
    	machine-readable output
  -once
    	start, make one request (GET /; for an MCP app an initialize to its route), print it and exit (smoke test)
  -port int
    	local port (127.0.0.1) (default 8787)
  -state-dir string
    	state directory (default $TWD_STATE_DIR or ~/.twd)
  -test-scheduled
    	serve /__scheduled?cron=<expr>[&time=<ms>] on the local port: run a cron trigger's scheduled() now
  -v	hostd logs to stderr
  -workerd string
    	workerd binary
  -wrangler
    	bundle with the wrangler CLI (wrangler deploy --dry-run --outdir; nothing is sent to Cloudflare) instead of the built-in esbuild
```

### twd types

generate Env types from twd.jsonc and wrangler config

```text
twd types: write the app's TypeScript Env (vars, Durable Object, KV, R2, D1, Queue and Workflow bindings, secret names) from its wrangler config and twd.jsonc, like wrangler types; --check fails when the file is stale (CI)

usage: twd types [dir] [--env <name>] [--out worker-configuration.d.ts] [--check] [--remote]

flags:
  -check
    	write nothing; fail (types_stale) if the file is missing or differs from what twd types would write (for CI)
  -env string
    	wrangler environment: type env.<name> from the wrangler config, as 'twd deploy --env' deploys it
  -json
    	machine-readable output
  -out string
    	the declaration file to write, relative to the app directory (default "worker-configuration.d.ts")
  -remote
    	also declare the workload's secrets from mgmt (the names 'twd secret ls' lists); needs a running or linked twd
  -state-dir string
    	state directory (default $TWD_STATE_DIR or ~/.twd)
  -tenant string
    	tenant: its tailnet, tenant ID or tailnet label (default: the 'twd up' tenant)
```

### twd mcp

twd's MCP server for coding agents (stdio)

```text
twd mcp: twd's MCP server for coding agents, over stdio (a bridge to mgmt's /mcp; tools: whoami status ls logs audit, and deploy kill undeploy when allowed); --config prints how to register it

usage: twd mcp [--allow deploy,kill,undeploy] | mcp --config

flags:
  -allow string
    	also allow these tools: deploy, kill, undeploy (comma-separated). On the twd host this is what enables them; from a linked machine your twd.dev/cap/mcp grant decides, and this only narrows
  -config
    	print how to register twd's MCP server with a coding agent, and exit
  -json
    	machine-readable output
  -state-dir string
    	state directory (default $TWD_STATE_DIR or ~/.twd)
```

## Deploy

### twd deploy

bundle, place and deploy an app; wait until ready

```text
twd deploy: bundle, preflight grants, build + push Dockerfile container images (docker buildx), place (prints why), deploy, wait until ready; --replace re-places a running workload; --preview runs it next to the workload instead (twd promote)

usage: twd deploy [dir] [--tenant <tailnet>] [--name <workload>] [--env <name>] [--wrangler | --from-wrangler-out <dir>] [--host <id>] [--replace] [--force-takeover] [--allow-missing-grants] [--no-wait] [--platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64] [--wait-public 5m] [--preview] [--preview-alias <alias>]

flags:
  -allow-missing-grants
    	deploy even if tailnet.connects grants are missing
  -env string
    	wrangler environment: use env.<name> from the wrangler config, as 'wrangler --env' does (the workload is named <name>-<env> unless the env sets a name)
  -force-takeover
    	the workload's current host is gone for good: move its Durable Objects anyway (audited; see takeover_unconfirmed); with --replace, confirms moving a stateful workload off a live host
  -from-wrangler-out string
    	deploy a bundle wrangler already built (the --outdir of 'wrangler deploy --dry-run')
  -host string
    	pin the workload to this host (it must be live, in the tenant's pool and offer the tier)
  -json
    	machine-readable output
  -name string
    	workload name (default: twd.jsonc name)
  -no-wait
    	return once mgmt accepted the deploy
  -platform string
    	containers: arches to build Dockerfile images for (linux/amd64,linux/arm64; default: the arches of the tenant pool's container hosts)
  -preview
    	deploy as a preview next to the workload (<workload>--preview-<alias>), leaving the workload as it is; twd promote makes it the workload
  -preview-alias string
    	the preview's alias (implies --preview; default: the start of the bundle's SHA-256)
  -replace
    	re-place the workload: move it to a clearly better host (smart placement: the best measured path to tailnet.connects) instead of keeping it where it runs
  -state-dir string
    	state directory (default $TWD_STATE_DIR or ~/.twd)
  -tenant string
    	tenant: its tailnet, tenant ID or tailnet label (default: the 'twd up' tenant)
  -var value
    	override a wrangler var (KEY=VALUE, repeatable)
  -wait duration
    	how long to wait for ready (default 3m0s)
  -wait-public duration
    	also wait (up to this long) until the public URL answers from the public internet (twd.jsonc "public")
  -wrangler
    	bundle with the wrangler CLI (wrangler deploy --dry-run --outdir; nothing is sent to Cloudflare) instead of the built-in esbuild
```

### twd deployments

a workload's deployment history

```text
twd deployments: a workload's deployment history, newest first: id, created, bundle sha256, status, host, who deployed (mgmt keeps the newest bundles for rollback)

usage: twd deployments <workload> [--tenant <tailnet>] [--limit N]

flags:
  -json
    	machine-readable output
  -limit int
    	show the newest N deployments (0 = all) (default 20)
  -state-dir string
    	state directory (default $TWD_STATE_DIR or ~/.twd)
  -tenant string
    	tenant: its tailnet, tenant ID or tailnet label (default: the 'twd up' tenant)
```

a workload's running preview deploys

```text
twd previews: a workload's running previews (twd deploy --preview): alias, created, bundle sha256, status, host, URL

usage: twd previews <workload> [--tenant <tailnet>]

flags:
  -json
    	machine-readable output
  -state-dir string
    	state directory (default $TWD_STATE_DIR or ~/.twd)
  -tenant string
    	tenant: its tailnet, tenant ID or tailnet label (default: the 'twd up' tenant)
```

### twd promote

make a preview the workload's deployment

```text
twd promote: deploy a preview's bundle to the workload as a new deployment, then undeploy the preview; code and config only, the workload keeps its data and secrets

usage: twd promote <workload> <preview> [--tenant <tailnet>] [--host <id>] [--replace] [--force-takeover] [--keep-preview] [--allow-missing-grants] [--no-wait]

flags:
  -allow-missing-grants
    	promote even if the current policy lacks grants the preview's bundle needs
  -force-takeover
    	as twd deploy --force-takeover
  -host string
    	pin the workload to this host (as twd deploy --host)
  -json
    	machine-readable output
  -keep-preview
    	leave the preview running (default: undeploy it once promoted)
  -no-wait
    	return once mgmt accepted the promotion
  -replace
    	re-place the workload (as twd deploy --replace); by default it stays on its host, with its Durable Object storage
  -state-dir string
    	state directory (default $TWD_STATE_DIR or ~/.twd)
  -tenant string
    	tenant: its tailnet, tenant ID or tailnet label (default: the 'twd up' tenant)
  -wait duration
    	how long to wait for ready (default 3m0s)
```

### twd rollback

redeploy an earlier deployment's bundle

```text
twd rollback: redeploy an earlier deployment's stored bundle as a new deployment (default: the previous one that ran); code and config only, data and secrets stay as they are now

usage: twd rollback <workload> [<deployment>] [--tenant <tailnet>] [--host <id>] [--replace] [--force-takeover] [--allow-missing-grants] [--no-wait]

flags:
  -allow-missing-grants
    	roll back even if the current policy lacks grants the old bundle needs
  -force-takeover
    	as twd deploy --force-takeover
  -host string
    	pin the rolled-back workload to this host (as twd deploy --host)
  -json
    	machine-readable output
  -no-wait
    	return once mgmt accepted the rollback
  -replace
    	re-place the workload (as twd deploy --replace); by default it stays on its host, with its Durable Object storage
  -state-dir string
    	state directory (default $TWD_STATE_DIR or ~/.twd)
  -tenant string
    	tenant: its tailnet, tenant ID or tailnet label (default: the 'twd up' tenant)
  -wait duration
    	how long to wait for ready (default 3m0s)
```

### twd undeploy

stop a workload and release its lease

```text
twd undeploy: stop a workload: kill its objects (cascade), release its lease

usage: twd undeploy <workload> [--tenant <tailnet>] [--reason <text>]

flags:
  -json
    	machine-readable output
  -reason string
    	why (recorded in audit)
  -state-dir string
    	state directory (default $TWD_STATE_DIR or ~/.twd)
  -tenant string
    	tenant: its tailnet, tenant ID or tailnet label (default: the 'twd up' tenant)
```

### twd expose

open or close a workload's public routes

```text
twd expose: open or close a workload's public (Funnel) routes; survives redeploys (twd.jsonc "public", ADR-029)

usage: twd expose on|off <workload> [--tenant <tailnet>]

flags:
  -json
    	machine-readable output
  -state-dir string
    	state directory (default $TWD_STATE_DIR or ~/.twd)
  -tenant string
    	tenant: its tailnet, tenant ID or tailnet label (default: the 'twd up' tenant)
```

### twd d1

a workload's D1 databases and migrations

```text
twd d1: a workload's D1 databases (like wrangler d1): create, list, delete, run SQL, export, and wrangler-layout migrations; execute/export/migrations reach the running workload

usage: twd d1 create <db> | d1 list | d1 delete <db> --yes | d1 execute <db> --command <sql> | --file <file> | d1 export <db> [--output <file>] | d1 migrations create <db> <message> | d1 migrations list <db> | d1 migrations apply <db>   [--workload <workload>] [--tenant <tailnet>]
  (every command takes --state-dir, default ~/.twd, and --json)
```

#### twd d1 create

```text
flags:
  -command string
    	execute: SQL to run (one or more statements, run as one batch)
  -file string

  -json
    	machine-readable output
  -output string
    	export: write the SQL to this file (default: stdout)
  -state-dir string
    	state directory (default $TWD_STATE_DIR or ~/.twd)
  -tenant string
    	tenant: its tailnet, tenant ID or tailnet label (default: the 'twd up' tenant)
```

### twd kv

a workload's Workers KV namespaces and keys

```text
twd kv: a workload's Workers KV namespaces (kv_namespaces, like wrangler kv): key commands name the namespace by --binding (from the wrangler config) or --namespace; writes reach running workloads within 60 s

usage: twd kv namespace create <NAME> | kv namespace list | kv namespace delete <NAME> | kv key put <KEY> [VALUE] [--path FILE] [--ttl S] [--expiration T] [--metadata JSON] | kv key get <KEY> | kv key delete <KEY> | kv key list [--prefix P]   [--binding <BINDING> or --namespace <NAME>] [--workload <workload>] [--tenant <tailnet>]

flags:
  -binding string
    	key commands: the namespace bound as this binding in the app's wrangler.jsonc
  -expiration int
    	key put: expire at this Unix time (≥ 60 s ahead)
  -json
    	machine-readable output
  -metadata string
    	key put: metadata (JSON, ≤ 1024 bytes)
  -namespace string
    	key commands: the namespace's name (its kv_namespaces id)
  -path string
    	key put: read the value from this file
  -prefix string
    	key list: only keys starting with this
  -state-dir string
    	state directory (default $TWD_STATE_DIR or ~/.twd)
  -tenant string
    	tenant: its tailnet, tenant ID or tailnet label (default: the 'twd up' tenant)
  -ttl int
    	key put: expire after this many seconds (≥ 60)
  -workload string
    	workload whose namespaces these are (default: the app in the current directory)
```

### twd queues

the tenant's queues: create, peek, send

```text
twd queues: the tenant's queues (like wrangler queues): producers' first send creates a queue; messages peeks without claiming (read a dead-letter queue); send takes JSON (or --text) from the argument or stdin

usage: twd queues create <queue> | queues ls | queues info <queue> | queues rm <queue> | queues purge <queue> | queues messages <queue> [--limit N] | queues send <queue> [<json>|--text <text>] [--delay S]   [--tenant <tailnet>]
  (every command takes --state-dir, default ~/.twd, and --json)
```

#### twd queues create

```text
flags:
  -delay int
    	send: delaySeconds (0-43200)
  -json
    	machine-readable output
  -limit int
    	messages: at most this many (1-100) (default 20)
  -state-dir string
    	state directory (default $TWD_STATE_DIR or ~/.twd)
  -tenant string
    	tenant: its tailnet, tenant ID or tailnet label (default: the 'twd up' tenant)
  -text
    	send: the body is text (contentType text), not JSON
```

```text
    	machine-readable output
  -limit int
    	messages: at most this many (1-100) (default 20)
  -state-dir string
    	state directory (default $TWD_STATE_DIR or ~/.twd)
  -tenant string
    	tenant: its tailnet, tenant ID or tailnet label (default: the 'twd up' tenant)
  -text
    	send: the body is text (contentType text), not JSON
```

### twd ls

list deployments and objects

```text
twd ls: list deployments and objects (paged; --all follows every page and shows killed objects)

usage: twd ls [--tenant <tailnet>] [--all] [--limit N]

flags:
  -all
    	include killed objects, and fetch every page
  -json
    	machine-readable output
  -limit int
    	at most this many objects (pages of ≤500 are followed up to it; --all lifts the cap) (default 200)
  -state-dir string

  -tenant string
```

### twd telemetry

the tenant's OTLP export

```text
twd telemetry: the tenant's OTLP export of request records, metrics and spans (each workload exports from its own node); --header NAME reads a credential from stdin, never shown again

usage: twd telemetry [show] | telemetry set --otlp <url> [--header NAME[=VALUE]]... [--signals logs,metrics,traces] | telemetry rm   [--tenant <tailnet>]

flags:
  -header value
    	set: a header for every export, NAME=VALUE, or NAME alone to read its value from stdin (repeatable)
  -json
    	machine-readable output
  -otlp string
    	set: the OTLP/HTTP base URL of a collector on the tailnet (http://otel-collector:4318)
  -signals string
    	set: what to export, comma-separated (default logs,metrics,traces)
  -state-dir string
    	state directory (default $TWD_STATE_DIR or ~/.twd)
  -tenant string
    	tenant: its tailnet, tenant ID or tailnet label (default: the 'twd up' tenant)
```

### twd audit

the hash-chained audit trail

```text
twd audit: show the hash-chained audit trail

usage: twd audit [--tenant <tailnet>] <object> | --human <login> | --trace <id> | --all

flags:
  -all
    	every record of the tenant
  -human string
    	records acting for this principal (login or caller node)
  -json
    	machine-readable output
  -state-dir string
    	state directory (default $TWD_STATE_DIR or ~/.twd)
  -tenant string
    	tenant: its tailnet, tenant ID or tailnet label (default: the 'twd up' tenant)
  -trace string
    	records of one trace
```

### twd logs

request records and console lines; daemon logs

```text
twd logs: show a workload's request records (one line per request with its console.* lines; --json, filters; --console for the raw app output), else the daemons' logs

usage: twd logs [workload] [--tenant <tailnet>] [--component mgmt|hostd|supervisor] [--host <id>] [-n 50] [-f] [--json] [--console] [--object <id|Class/name>] [--status 5xx] [--outcome exception] [--errors] [--caller <login|node>] [--trace <id>]

flags:
  -caller string
    	only callers whose login or node name contains this (public: Funnel requests)
  -component string
    	mgmt | hostd | supervisor (default: hostd, or workerd for a workload)
  -console
    	the app's raw output (workerd.log, the node tier's app.log, the microVM console) instead of request records
  -errors
    	only errors (status ≥ 400, an outcome other than ok, or an exception)
  -f	follow
  -host string
    	linked machine: only the replica on this host
  -json
    	machine-readable output
  -n int
    	lines (default 50)
  -object string
    	only this object (object ID, Class/name, Class or name)
  -outcome string
    	only this outcome (ok, exception, canceled, …)
  -state-dir string
    	state directory (default $TWD_STATE_DIR or ~/.twd)
  -status string
    	only this status (404) or class (5xx)
  -tenant string
    	tenant: its tailnet, tenant ID or tailnet label (default: the 'twd up' tenant)
  -trace string
    	only this trace ID (or a prefix), or audit trace ID
```

### twd approve

approve or reject a waiting Workflow

```text
twd approve: approve (or --reject) a waiting Workflow as your own tailnet identity (needs a twd.dev/cap/approve grant; from a `twd link`ed machine)

usage: twd approve <workload> <instance> [--reject] [--comment <text>] [--workflow <name>] [--step <name>] [--tenant <tailnet>]

flags:
  -comment string
    	shown to the Workflow and recorded in the audit log
  -json
    	machine-readable output
  -reject
    	reject instead of approve
  -state-dir string
    	state directory (default $TWD_STATE_DIR or ~/.twd)
  -step string
    	which wait, when the instance waits for several
  -tenant string
    	tenant: its tailnet, tenant ID or tailnet label (default: the 'twd up' tenant)
  -workflow string
    	the Workflow's name (default: the one whose instance waits)
```

a webhook for approvals waiting for a decision

```text
  -tenant string

  -webhook string
    	set: the URL mgmt POSTs to (https://hooks.slack.com/services/…, http://chat-bot/notify); - reads it from stdin
```

### twd upgrade

upgrade twd on this machine or the fleet

```text
twd upgrade: upgrade twd: on a twd up machine, back up, install a newer release and roll back if it isn't healthy; against a linked twd-mgmt (or --fleet), plan and run a fleet upgrade (status, pause, resume, abort)

usage: twd upgrade [<version>] [--from <tarball|dir>] [--plan] [--yes] [--fleet] [--hosts h1,h2] [--canary h] [--soak 5m] [--settle 5m] [--no-wait] | upgrade status|pause|resume|abort [<run-id>]

flags:
  -canary string
    	fleet: the canary host (default: the first)
  -fleet
    	upgrade the fleet through twd-mgmt (an upgrade run) even on a twd up machine
  -from string
    	install this release tarball (twd-<v>-<os>-<arch>.tar.gz, with SHA256SUMS next to it) or extracted release directory instead of downloading
  -health-timeout duration
    	homelab: how long the upgraded twd may take to report healthy before it is rolled back (default 3m0s)
  -hosts string
    	fleet: only these hosts (comma-separated)
  -json
    	machine-readable output
  -no-rollback
    	homelab: keep the new release even if the health check fails
  -no-wait
    	fleet: start the run and return (twd upgrade status follows it)
  -plan
    	print the plan and change nothing
  -prefix string
    	homelab: the install.sh prefix to upgrade (default: the one that owns --state-dir)
  -settle duration
    	fleet: how long a host may take to come back and settle (default 5m0s)
  -soak duration
    	fleet: watch the canary this long before the other hosts (default 5m0s)
  -state-dir string
    	state directory (default $TWD_STATE_DIR or ~/.twd)
  -yes
    	don't ask for confirmation
```
